events_chronological: Kes phones Mira in a panic: he has left eighty thousand in a bag on the train and has twenty minutes to hand it to his boss Vart.
Mira runs out of the flat past her mother on the telephone and down the stairwell past a woman with a pram and a growling dog.
Mira reaches her father's bank and finds him with his mistress Elke, who has just told him she is pregnant.
Her father denies her the money, tells her he is not her father at all, and has her put out of the building.
Mira arrives too late; Kes has robbed a supermarket, and in the getaway a policeman shoots Mira dead.
In the second attempt Mira is tripped on the stairs and reaches the bank a moment later.
Her father, mid-argument with Elke, slaps her, and Mira takes the security guard's gun and robs the bank herself.
Mira gets out with the money and finds Kes, who is run over by an ambulance in front of her.
In the third attempt Mira is a moment earlier on the stairs and misses her father entirely, seeing him drive away with his colleague Vogl.
Mira walks into a casino, buys a single chip, and screams the roulette ball onto the same number twice to win far more than she needs.
This time Kes spots the tramp who took his bag and chases him down on foot.
Kes gets the money back at gunpoint and hands it to Vart with seconds to spare.
Mira arrives carrying a bag of her own, and Kes asks what is in it.
Between the attempts, Mira and Kes lie in bed in red light asking each other whether the other really loves them.
Each attempt rewrites the futures of the strangers Mira passes - the woman with the pram, an office worker called Hanne, a cyclist - shown in bursts of snapshots.
Her father's fate diverges every time: publicly exposed, robbed by his own daughter, or killed in a crash with Vogl.
nonlinear_category_reason: The same twenty minutes is run three times as separate blocks, with the bedroom interludes and the strangers' futures set outside all three.
syuzhet_notes: The film plays the same twenty minutes three times over, restarting from the telephone call after each ending, so told-order bullets 8 and 11 are hard resets that put the story back where it stood at bullet 2. The two deaths at told-order bullets 6 and 10 are both undone by the next restart, and bullet 7 is a bedroom scene that belongs to none of the three attempts.
fabula_notes: The three attempts are alternatives rather than a sequence, so this ordering lays them out as successive tries instead of one causal chain; nothing carries between them except the protagonist's apparent memory of having done it before. The snapshot futures of the passers-by are flash-forwards decades ahead, and they differ every time.
